desc:
Dashboard performance tuning and slow query fixes make heavy screens load faster. Ecom Swift LLC measures where your dashboard loses time, applies the safest fixes in your own project and gives you a written before and after report.

## What is dashboard performance tuning?

Dashboard performance tuning is the work of finding why a screen is slow and fixing the causes. The causes usually sit in a few places: database queries that scan too much data, a page that sends dozens of requests, large files delivered to the browser, or charts that redraw more often than needed.

Tuning begins with measurement. Guessing leads to changes that feel productive and fix nothing, so we time the real screens first.

## Why slow screens cost you users and staff time

A slow dashboard is a daily tax. Customers wait for numbers, lose their train of thought and open fewer reports. Staff sit watching a spinner while a customer waits on the phone. People rarely complain about speed directly. They just use the product less, or they build workarounds such as exporting data and working in spreadsheets.

Slowness also tends to grow. A query that was fine with a few hundred rows becomes painful with a few hundred thousand. Fixing it early is cheaper than fixing it after customers have started to leave.

## What a good tune-up covers

- Timing of each target screen, from request to fully drawn page.
- A list of the slowest database queries and what makes them slow.
- Indexes added where they are safe and useful.
- Caching for numbers that are requested often and change slowly.
- Fewer requests per screen, by combining or removing calls.
- Data loaded only when it is needed, such as when a tab is opened.
- Smaller files sent to the browser, including scripts and images.
- Charts and tables that redraw only when their data changes.
- Alerts for slow queries, so new problems are caught early.
- A written report with real timings before and after.

## How we work

First we agree on the screens that hurt most. We measure them in a test or staging copy of your app and record load times, query times and request counts. From the numbers, we rank the problems by how much time each one costs.

Then we apply the fixes in your project, starting with the safest and biggest. We test after each change to confirm that the screen behaves the same and the timing improves. The Basic package measures one slow screen and applies the top fixes. Standard covers several screens, adds indexes and caching, and delivers a findings report. Premium adds slow query alerts, a review of front-end size and loading, and a plan for how the app should cope as data grows. We cannot promise a specific speed, because it depends on your data, hosting and code, but you will see the measured change.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Measure before changing anything.
- Fix the biggest cost first.
- Test with realistic amounts of data.
- Cache numbers that do not need to be live.
- Keep a record of timings so you can spot regressions.

**Avoid:**
- Adding indexes everywhere without checking.
- Caching data that must always be current.
- Tuning on tiny sample data that hides the problem.
- Upgrading hosting before finding the real cause.
- Changing many things at once, so you cannot tell what helped.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS teams whose reports take too long to open and founders hearing complaints about speed. It suits a developer who knows a screen is slow but has no time to investigate, and a growing product whose data has outgrown its first design. It is also useful before a launch or a big customer onboarding.

## What we need from you

Tell us which screens feel slow and how users describe the problem. Send a staging link or a test copy of your app and its data, and say how your app is hosted.

We need developer or collaborator access to your code repository and a test database. We do not need live customer data, and we never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until the report is delivered.
